architectureReview.summary: Independent architect review found reasonless archive fencing/retry paths, endpoint-derived authority remaining in live Telegram/TopicRegistry state, Router-memory-only cleanup receipts, a legacy callback seam, Telegram-local teardown capable of terminalizing turn state, recovery awaiting Telegram Bot API terminalization, and no real Telegram+ACP/MCP sibling containment fixture.
architectureReview.evidence: Read-only review by architect agent 4-Issue4399ArchitectReview against frozen source; no source changes made.

blockers: Plan/code mismatch: mandatory matrix requires real provider-local Telegram failure alongside unaffected ACP, MCP, SDK authority, and active turn; added tests are a synthetic Router/TopicRegistry harness and do not exercise real Telegram daemon plus siblings.

Provider boundary remains incomplete: SessionAttachment with retire/isCurrent/endpoint identity is still a generic provider-facing capability, Telegram retains a legacy test adapter accepting it, and generic onSessionRemoved/onFrame hooks remain injectable.

Durable authority mismatch: TopicRegistry.load recreates endpointKey/sessionId and endpointDigest/telegram for Telegram bindings, while live Telegram lease/replay/admission logic still compares endpointKey, endpointGeneration, attachmentKey, and hostGeneration.

Telegram-local teardown still runs turn-affecting cleanup (cancelLegacyToolStartsForSession, terminalize Btw/tool activity, revoke callback aliases, release topic lease) in #dropSession; this violates the absolute Telegram-only failure invariant.
Router cleanup receipts are process-memory only; the contract requires provider-local durable pending/failed receipts. No artifact or test proves persistence/recovery of these receipts.

Archive authority remains coupled to provider lifecycle and remote Bot API: explicit session_closed/create compensation paths still perform archive work, and architect review reports recovery can await Telegram terminalization.
